messages:
emma: Heads-up: after the selector tweak on A2 I observed a persistent p95 TTFT uptick in our replay runs. Need a compact SOP that defines TTFT/TPOT/qps/goodput and a reproducible AB matrix so infra folks stop chasing noise.

liam: Which runs? link or run ids please.

emma: perf-harness run 2143654310 (replay-2025-nov, kv=on, selector=auto-v4). Baseline p95=39ms -> post-change p95=47ms. Synthetic generator (uniform seq len 128) shows no delta.

maya: That smells like batch-shape mismatch + kv-hit interplay. Replay has lots of prefix reuse -> many tiny batches. Selector might be picking a kernel with higher launch overhead but better big-batch throughput.

jordan: We should put canonical metric definitions in the thread so all teams quote the same numbers. My proposal (explicit names to avoid client/runtime confusion):
- server_ttft: runtime-arrival -> first token byte emitted by the model worker. Includes scheduling + kernel exec + kv lookup. Excludes client RTT and CDN.
- tp_token_ms: per-token interarrival after first token (report median, p95, p99). For streaming, aggregate token samples across the measurement window. Use 95% trimmed mean for central tendency.
- qps_runtime: completed requests/sec measured at runtime completion event.
- goodput_toks_s: tokens/sec that required model evaluation (exclude tokens satisfied entirely from KV). Report both absolute and per-GPU-normalized values.

benchbot: AUTO: queued run_id=2143654310 cfg={selector:auto-v4,batcher:fixed_25ms_64,kv_prewarm:true,seq_profile:replay-2025-11} server_ttft_p95=47.0ms server_ttft_p50=11.8ms tp_token_median=4.1ms goodput=110k_tok/s gpu_util=71%

liam: For apples-to-apples comparisons we must control the following knobs explicitly in the harness:
1) force-selector/force-kernel flag so selection branching is disabled.
2) batcher: deterministic policy (batch-window-ms + max-batch).
3) kv prewarm: bring prefix hit-rate to a target (e.g., 80-90%) before measurement.
4) seq-dist: synthetic generators must match replay's empirical histogram, not just the mean.
5) measurement windows: fixed warmup + measurement durations (e.g., 10m warmup, 15m measure) and drop initial 10s of the measure window.

maya: Add NVTX ranges for the "first-token" path and collect kernel launch latency histograms, SASS stall metrics, and memcpy timing. TTFT tails commonly correlate with memcpy/launch stalls.

emma: Aggregation rules: compute metrics only over the measurement window. For tp_token use 95% trimmed mean, but keep raw p95/p99 for tails. Report both absolute goodput and goodput per GPU.

jordan: Derived signals to collect:
- kv_hit_rate_by_route (tagged by route_id)
- batch_size_histogram (buckets: 1,2,3,4,5-8,9-16,17-32,33-64)
- selector_choice_counts (how many times each kernel was chosen)
These should be emitted per-min and attached to run artifacts.

liam: Hypothesis: the new selector picks kernel K_long with slightly higher per-launch overhead. In replay many requests end up in tiny batches (median batch < 8) so that overhead shows up in p95 TTFT. Synthetic had median batch ~32 so overhead amortized away.

maya: Experiments to validate:
- A/B forced kernel runs on the same replay trace with identical batching and kv prewarm.
- Run with kv disabled (kv_off) to see if delta disappears.
- Reconfigure synthetic generator to emulate prefix-reuse bursts (short sequences and high prefix hit patterns) and re-run.

emma: Example perf command to run the A/B with the SOP knobs:
```
./perf_harness \
  --trace replay-2025-11.json \
  --force-kernel=K_stable \
  --batch-window-ms=25 --max-batch=64 \
  --kv-prewarm=85 --warm-sec=600 --measure-sec=900 \
  --collect-nvtx --emit=server_ttft,tp_token_ms,qps_runtime,goodput_toks_s,kv_hit_rate,batch_hist,selector_choice
```

benchbot: SCHEDULED: run_ids=[2143654322_AB,2143654323_AB] start=2143658000

liam: I'll ensure per-request selector_choice & batch_size get written to s3 for correlation analysis. Also will capture GPU timelines and /proc metrics.

jordan: I'll add kv_hit_rate_by_route and batch_size_histogram to the metrics pipeline and prefix server_ttft metric as "server_ttft" so dashboards don't conflate with client_ttft.

maya: If the A/B confirms K_long tail, mitigation options: (1) tune K_long to reduce launch/shared-mem footprint, (2) bias selector heuristics to avoid K_long for small-batch regimes, or (3) tweak batching to coalesce where safe.

emma: Rollout gate suggestion: any selector or kernel change must pass a 1h replay A/B with the SOP controls. Acceptance criteria: server_ttft_p95 delta < 5% and tp_token_p99 must not regress. Otherwise block rollout.

sam: Quick nit: ensure the harness emits both "server_ttft" and "client_ttft" labels and that dashboards plot them side-by-side so ops can triage network vs runtime issues.

benchbot: RESULTS_POST: run=2143654322 (force=K_stable) server_ttft_p95=39.3ms run=2143654323 (force=K_long) server_ttft_p95=48.8ms batch_median=7 kv_hit=84% flamegraphs=s3://perf-artifacts/21436543/*

emma: That's pretty decisive. Maya, please prepare selector patch that biases against K_long when recent median batch <= 8 and add a perf test to CI that runs the synthetic prefix-reuse mode.

maya: On it. I'll also add a short SOP doc to the repo with the 5 knobs and the AB gating criteria.

liam: I'll upload the raw logs and flamegraphs to the run artifact folder and tag the rollback ticket if we want an immediate mitigation.

jordan: I'll wire up dashboard panels: server_ttft (p50/p95/p99), tp_token_ms (p50/p95/p99), goodput per GPU, kv_hit_rate_by_route, batch_size_histogram, and selector_choice breakdown.

emma: Thanks all. Keeping this thread for all artifacts and decisions. :thumbsup:
